items.title: World leaders hope for reset after US midterms
items.summary: Germany German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said he hoped to see new initiatives to end the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine. Spain Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said Trump's defeat showed that the global far-right was on the wane. Russia Russia hopes Trump will continue his "peacemaking efforts" after the midterm elections, the Kremlin said.

items.title: Sharp metal objects found in Halloween sweets in Austria
items.summary: VIENNA: Austrian police have launched an investigation after small metal objects such as nails, needles and pins were found in Halloween sweets at several locations across the country. German authorities this week also reported several cases of small metal objects being found inside Halloween sweets. Austrian police have received 13 reports of metal objects found in sweets collected by children at Halloween, federal criminal police said on Wednesday in a statement sent to AFP.

items.title: Singapore toughens haze law, raises maximum fine tenfold to S$20mil
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore's parliament passed amendments to the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act (THPA), introducing higher maximum fines and stronger investigative and enforcement powers against entities responsible for cross-border haze. Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu said the amendments would strengthen Singapore's standing as a jurisdiction with credible and robust environmental standards. Meanwhile, Singapore Institute of International Affairs chairman Simon Tay said the amendments would strengthen penalties against companies responsible for transboundary haze.

items.title: UK man tells rape trial he thought snoring woman was 'roleplaying'
items.summary: LONDON: A UK man accused of raping a woman whose husband invited strangers to have sex with her told a court Wednesday he heard her snoring but thought she was "roleplaying." Wilkins and three other men are standing trial at a court in southern England accused of various sexual offences committed jointly with the husband against Joanne Young. Young has admitted multiple counts of drugging and raping her over 13 years.

items.title: Seven foreigners arrested, RM1.08mil worth of drugs seized in Bukit Mertajam
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Police arrested seven foreigners and seized suspected methylenedioxy methamphetamine (MDMA) powder and ketamine worth RM1.08 million during raids on two premises in Bukit Tengah here on Nov 1. Seberang Perai Tengah police chief assistant commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said a team from the district Narcotics Crime Investigation Department raided the premises at 12.50am following surveillance and intelligence gathering. Nik Aminuddin said urine screening tests revealed that two of the suspects tested positive for methamphetamine, while the other five tested negative.

items.title: Elon Musk's business empire braces for Democratic wave as Texas flips blue
items.summary: WASHINGTON: As Republicans suffered a landslide defeat and Texas elected its first Democratic governor in more than three decades, one of the biggest losers of the US midterms was not on the ballot: billionaire Elon Musk. The world's richest man spent nearly half a billion dollars to back Republican candidates and keep Texas red - a state home to his automaker Tesla, rocket-to-AI company SpaceX and a planned chipmaking venture between the two. Those bets unravelled as Democrats seized both chambers of Congress and Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott in the Texas governor's race, in a stinging rebuke to US President Donald Trump, a close Musk ally whom the billionaire helped elect.

items.title: Democrat El-Sayed hails win amid blue 'tsunami'
items.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has won Michigan's United States Senate race over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. "Michigan, we did it!" The Michigan medical administrator rallied voters on leftist campaign promises, including universal healthcare, to win a key Senate seat for Democrats, taking over from the retiring Gary Peters.

items.title: US midterm voters deliver brutal verdict on Trump
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Donald Trump faced a radically transformed and hostile political landscape on Wednesday after US voters handed control of Congress to the Democrats in a stunning rebuke to his presidency. The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept into his Republican heartland, boosted by anger at soaring energy costs and his costly, dragging war with Iran. The Democratic capture of both the Senate and the House of Representatives signals an end to Trump's stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, launch investigations into Trump's administration and thwart his appointments.

items.title: Will lame duck Trump cause a flap after the midterms?
items.summary: Donald Trump struck a surprisingly conciliatory tone after the Democratic sweep of the United States midterm elections rendered him a lame-duck president. From renewed military action against Iran to vetoing Democratic legislation, the volatile 80-year-old could still use his remaining powers to cause major disruption in his last two years in office. VETOES AND EXECUTIVE POWER Trump congratulated the Democrats on Tuesday and said he would be ready to work with them.

items.title: China seeks arrest of five Uyghurs held in Thailand
items.summary: BANGKOK: Five Uyghurs detained in Thailand since 2014 are subject to Chinese arrest warrants, the kingdom's security chief said Wednesday, adding that a court would decide if they would be returned to China. Human rights groups have raised concerns about the men – members of the Muslim minority group who activists say are persecuted in China – after two of them were pardoned by Thailand last month. He said that if China requests their extradition, Thailand's foreign ministry would make an assessment and a court would then decide.

items.title: NST Leader: A lesson from Penang
items.summary: The 1993 Highland Towers tragedy claimed 48 lives. The incident prompted greater attention to regulations governing hillside development, slope maintenance and disaster-response coordination. Recurring concerns surrounding hillside development in Penang serve as a reminder that the lessons of Highland Towers must never be forgotten.

items.title: UK parliament risks 'catastrophic failure' over delayed renovation
items.summary: LONDON: Britain's centuries-old parliament is at risk of a "Notre Dame-like" fire or other catastrophe if lawmakers continue to put off a major restoration project, MPs warned Wednesday. Billions of pounds are required to renovate the estate, which sits within a Unesco world heritage site, but parliamentarians have been unable to decide for years on how to proceed. Parliament's public accounts committee said the delay was leading to spiralling costs and risked causing a "catastrophic failure" that would harm the UK's "morale and reputation."

items.title: Transport Ministry working to resolve train congestion, technical issues, says Loke
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: The Transport Ministry is working to address train service congestion and resolve technical issues faced by rail operators, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke. We will resolve these technical issues to improve the service," he said. On Oct 30, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim directed the Transport Minister to swiftly resolve train congestion issues, expressing concern that they disrupt the public's daily routine.

items.title: Country Heights property auction draws no bidders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Country Heights Holdings Bhd's latest public auction of its property in Petaling Jaya has failed to attract bidders. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the public auction of the property belonging to Mines Waterfront Business Park Sdn Bhd was unsuccessful due to the absence of bidders. MBSB Bank Bhd initiated the auction, which took place on Wednesday at 9am via the e-Lelong platform.

items.title: Dollar and oil drop after Trump's election rout
items.summary: LONDON: The dollar and oil prices dropped on Wednesday as traders digested President Donald Trump's heavy defeat in US midterm elections that saw his Republican party lose control of Congress. "Investors are trying to get their heads around what a Democrat landslide means for financial markets," noted Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell. Technology firms also slumped amid suggestions Democrats could prioritise AI regulation.

items.title: Nga: Govt saves RM3bil by leasing 28 helicopters
items.summary: SUBANG: The government has saved RM3 billion through a leasing arrangement for 28 helicopters for use by various government agencies, including two AW139 units that have expanded the Fire and Rescue Department's fleet to 10 helicopters. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the leasing arrangement, instead of direct purchases, shifted maintenance responsibilities to the leasing company throughout the 15-year contract period. He said the two AW139 helicopters would strengthen the department's capabilities in search and rescue (SAR) operations, forest firefighting and the delivery of logistical aid.

items.title: Abang Johari given full mandate to decide on GPS candidates, says Uggah
items.summary: KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg has been given full mandate to decide on the coalition's candidates for the 13th Sarawak election. On Oct 23, Abang Johari, who is also Sarawak Premier, announced that the Sarawak state legislative assembly would be dissolved effective Oct 26. GPS comprises four component parties, namely PBB, Parti Rakyat Bersatu Sarawak (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and Parti Demokratik Progresif (PDP).

items.title: Indonesia to push for ratification of Asean haze centre agreement
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia will push for the ratification of an agreement to operationalise the Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control (ACCTHPC) at the 49th Asean Summit in Manila. Foreign Ministry Director-General for Asean Cooperation Ina Krisnamurthi said the centre already had a secretariat in Jakarta but could not begin operations until Asean member states ratified the agreement. "The centre must be up and running.

items.title: CAAM: Helicopter landed in Bintulu as precautionary measure
items.summary: Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the pilot made the landing as a precautionary measure. Norazman said the pilot landed the helicopter near the Sri Pertiwi housing estate in Kidurong, Bintulu, at 3.18pm. The pilot and two passengers are safe," he said.

items.title: MMEA investigating collision between local boat and unidentified vessel
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) is conducting further investigations into an incident involving a local fishing boat that was struck by another vessel in Terengganu waters. Terengganu Maritime director Captain Hamiludin Che Awang said based on a witness account, the incident occurred around 5am, approximately 33 nautical miles from the Kuala Terengganu estuary. None of the local fishing boat's crew members was injured," he said.

items.title: Aliff Daniel ordered to undergo three-month faith rehabilitation over improper worship
items.summary: RAWANG: A 21-year-old man who went viral for performing religious rituals at a temple in Batu Caves has been ordered to undergo three months of faith rehabilitation after pleading guilty to a charge of improper worship. The Syariah Lower Court ordered Aliff Daniel Adli to undergo rehabilitation at the Baitul Iman Faith Rehabilitation Centre in Ulu Yam, beginning today. Syariah judge Mohd Faizal Habib made the order under Section 54(1) of the Selangor Syariah Criminal Offences Enactment 1995, which allows the court to substitute imprisonment and fines with rehabilitation at an approved centre for up to six months.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - November 4, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Here are today's top stories. Google invests US$15bil Google will invest US$15 billion in Malaysia between 2027 and 2028 to expand its data centre infrastructure, boost clean energy and water security, and upskill 800,000 Malaysians by 2031. Shuhaily resumes duties Border agency chief Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has resumed work, visiting several posts along the Sarawak-Indonesia border.

items.title: One dead, two missing after Indonesian army helicopter crash during firefighting operations
items.summary: JAKARTA: One person was killed and two others remain missing after a Mi-17V5 helicopter belonging to the Indonesian Army crashed while conducting a forest firefighting operation in Central Kalimantan on Wednesday. The helicopter departed from Kuala Pembuang at 9.55 am towards Telaga Pulang before crashing while collecting water for a water bombing operation. The helicopter departed from Kuala Pembuang at 9.55am for Telaga Pulang before crashing while collecting water for a water-bombing operation.

items.title: Mercedes-Benz C-Class goes electric, priced from RM360,888
items.summary: MERCEDES-Benz Malaysia has opened pre-bookings for the all-new electric C-Class, with the C 300 4Matic electric AMG Line Plus carrying an estimated price starting from RM360,888. The electric saloon is the first fully electric version of the German marque's C-Class, one of its established model lines. An optional 22kW-capable onboard AC charging system is also available.

items.title: Govt to conduct cyber threat stress tests across sectors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will conduct a series of stress tests across various sectors to assess the country's preparedness against cyber threats, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) would also provide an early warning system capable of broadcasting official government information directly to mobile phones nationwide. He said the ministry was also tasked with assessing cybersecurity across the country's telecommunications and broadcasting networks, including those operated by Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) and Bernama.

items.title: Fadhlina warns of ‘scrolling generation’ as gadgets erode reading habits among youth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The emergence of digital gadgets has increasingly undermined reading habits among younger generations, giving rise to a “scrolling generation”, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said reading should be part of everyday life, rather than merely a leisure activity, to nurture a more knowledgeable generation. Fadhlina said encouraging a reading culture among Malaysians, particularly students at schools and universities, was a key government priority, adding that the ministry introduced the ‘Jom Baca Bersama 10 Minit’ programme to promote reading among pre-school, primary and secondary school pupils.

items.title: Sunway Construction's unit clinches RM920mil variation works contract in Johor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Construction Group Bhd's wholly owned unit Sunway Construction Sdn Bhd has received a letter of award for variation (LOAV) works from a US-headquartered multinational technology corporation worth approximately RM920.8 million. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the construction group said the variation works involve additional mechanical, electrical, and plumbing fit-out works for the ongoing development of a data centre in Johor. The group said the variation works contract will not affect the group's share capital or substantial shareholders' shareholdings, as no new shares will be allotted or issued under the variation works.

items.title: FDS still grounded amid reports of helicopter's emergency landing in Bintulu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Flying Doctor Service (FDS) in Sarawak has yet to resume operations and is still undergoing further scrutiny and assessment before any decision is made on its reactivation. The Health Ministry said any resumption of the service would have to take into account operational safety, the welfare of personnel and staff readiness. "The helicopter made an emergency landing due to a minor technical problem.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Price of RON97 down by 20 sen, RON95 and diesel drop by 15 sen respectively tomorrow
items.summary: Meanwhile, the price of subsidised RON95 through Budi95 remains at RM1.99 per liter, with the government bearing a subsidy of RM2.28 per liter, or 53 percent of the unsubsidised price for the period. For Budi Diesel, the price for eligible recipients remains at RM2.10 per liter, involving a government subsidy of RM3.02 per liter, or 59 percent of the unsubsidised price. Additionally, the price of petrol under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) remains at RM2.05 per liter, while diesel under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) remains at RM2.15 per liter.

items.title: 1,500 oil palm smallholders to benefit from replanting financing incentive scheme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,500 independent smallholders, covering 5,900ha, are expected to benefit from the Smallholder Oil Palm Replanting Financing Incentive Scheme (TSPKS) 2.0 under the 2027 Budget. Plantations and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad said the programme aims to support independent smallholders in replanting activities and strengthen the sustainability of the oil palm sector. "In addition, 740 independent oil palm smallholders, with a combined cultivation area of 11,110 hectares, are expected to benefit from the Oil Palm Replanting Financing Programme (PTSS)," she said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Penang e-hailing drivers to get one-off RM600 aid from 2027
items.summary: State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the application criteria for the Special E-Hailing Incentive Assistance would be announced next month. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, when tabling the 2027 State Budget on Friday (Oct 30), announced that the state government would introduce a one-off Special E-Hailing Incentive Assistance of RM600 for eligible drivers, with an allocation ceiling of RM9 million. The State Legislative Assembly sitting will resume tomorrow.

items.title: Melaka polls: No instructions from Bersatu to supporters to back PH
items.summary: MELAKA: Bersatu has not issued any instructions to its grassroots members to support Pakatan Harapan candidates in seats where there is no contest between the two coalitions in the Melaka election. Its vice-president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu said although the party had not issued any instructions to its members and supporters, it appreciated PH's willingness to support its candidates. Adly had previously said the coalition had no objection to its supporters backing Bersatu candidates in state seats it was not contesting.

items.title: Mutiara Line LRT link to Penang Sentral to begin construction in 2027, completion targeted for 2031
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — Construction of the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) alignment linking Macallum on the island to Penang Sentral in Seberang Perai, including a marine bridge across the Penang Strait, is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027. Preliminary works will be carried out first, followed by major construction activities, including the construction of a bridge across the Penang Strait. Zairil said the finalised Macallum-Penang Sentral alignment would feature a 5.5-kilometre (km) marine bridge across the Penang Strait, with two main stations at Macallum and Penang Sentral.

items.title: In Johor, six-year-old boy drowns after falling into reservoir while fishing
items.summary: KULAI, Nov 4 — A six-year-old boy drowned after falling into a reservoir while fishing at Jalan Budiman in Kampung Melayu Kulai here today. Kulai Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Awang Adzwan Awang Sahari said authorities received a distress call on the incident at 10.17am. Awang Adzwan said the team located the victim and carried out a rescue operation.

items.title: Over five million Malaysians to receive RM1.1b STR aid from today, says Anwar
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the disbursement is being made in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration and covers recipients from various ethnic backgrounds. Also present were Minister of Communications Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, and Minister of Digital Gobind Singh Deo. RM6 billion.

items.title: Selangor gears up for north-east monsoon, deploys 7,677 personnel for disaster response
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 4 — The Selangor state government has mobilised 7,677 personnel from various state agencies to prepare for disasters during the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to continue until March 2027. State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the mobilisation involved the State Disaster Management Unit (UPBN), local authorities, district offices and relevant agencies to coordinate operations and monitor high-risk areas. Jamaliah said JPS was monitoring flood risks through 221 rainfall telemetry stations, 124 water-level monitoring stations, 140 warning sirens and 72 IP cameras.

items.title: Klang Valley raids uncover suspected luxury liquor tax-stamp scam, RM702,566 haul seized
items.summary: He said initial inspections at the warehouse found that some luxury liquor bottles allegedly bore tax stamps or customs labels with lower duty rates than those applicable to the products. However, inspections at the second premises found that all liquor bottles bore valid tax stamps, with no offences detected. The Customs Department is also investigating possible offences under Section 133(1)(c) of the Customs Act 1967.

items.title: Three boat operators among 38 Indonesians held in Selangor migrant smuggling crackdown
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Three boat operators were among 38 Indonesian nationals detained by the General Operations Force (GOF) in an operation to curb migrant smuggling along the coastal area of Kampung Sungai Gatal, near Sabak Bernam, on November 2. He said the other 35 individuals arrested comprised 24 adult men and 11 adult women. Awang Arfian said the GOF Central Brigade recorded 171 cases involving migrant smuggling activities and immigration offences from January 1 to November 4 this year.

items.title: Anwar says aid for Indian community goes beyond Mitra, more initiatives in pipeline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Government assistance for the Indian community is not only channelled through the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), but also includes various initiatives in welfare, entrepreneurship, education and social development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said such assistance was also provided through various government agencies and programmes, including the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid scheme, Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), entrepreneurship financing through Tekun Nasional and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, as well as allocations for the development of Tamil schools and places of worship. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.

items.title: Malaysian prosecutors unable to find Yusoff Rawther in UK to physically serve appeal notice despite Interpol help
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 4 — The Court of Appeal was told today that the prosecution has yet to physically serve a notice of appeal on Muhammed Yusoff Rawther, a former research assistant to a politician, who is currently in the United Kingdom (UK). “The prosecution was informed last month that efforts to locate the respondent (Muhammed Yusoff) had been unsuccessful. The DPP said the prosecution was seeking another case management date to allow efforts to locate Muhammed Yusoff and serve the notice to continue.

items.title: Penang DOSH to probe cause of fatal Paya Terubong landslide, developer told to submit documents
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — The Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) is conducting an investigation to determine the actual cause of the landslide at Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, covering aspects such as safety, construction, and regulatory compliance. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the investigation includes gathering information and statements from the developer, contractors, and consultants involved in the development project on the slope near the site of the incident. “The Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) held discussions yesterday (Nov 3) with civil and geotechnical consulting engineers, the developer, and the contractor to investigate and understand the root cause of the incident covering aspects of safety, construction, design, and compliance with relevant regulations as well as to propose appropriate mitigation measures and site stabilization efforts.

items.title: Police arrest 35 foreigners in Penang love scam, gold investment fraud raids
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — Police arrested 35 foreign nationals suspected of involvement in an online fraud syndicate specialising in love scams and gold investment schemes during raids on two residences in Bayan Lepas, near here, last Monday. Barat Daya police chief ACP Anuwal Ab Wahab said the suspects, comprising 33 Chinese men, one Chinese woman and one Taiwanese man, were arrested in an operation conducted by the district’s Commercial Crime Investigation Division in collaboration with the Penang Contingent Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID). “Preliminary investigations revealed that the syndicate began operating last September, targeting Chinese national women aged between 18 and 46 through the Telegram application,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: HR minister: 864 employers, including VVIPs, MPs and assemblymen, fail to pay Socso for domestic workers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — A total of 864 high-profile individuals, including prominent figures (VVIPs), members of parliament and state assemblymen, have been identified for failing to pay Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributions for their domestic workers. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the figure was part of 10,033 employers of domestic workers found to have failed to comply with the contribution requirements, based on Perkeso’s preliminary checks as at November 1. Also present were Perkeso Board chairman Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal and Perkeso Group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed.

items.title: Sungai Buloh floods leave 306 people at three evacuation centres
items.summary: Sungai Buloh District Police Chief Supt Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said all the affected victims are from Kampung Kubu Gajah, Kampung Merbau Sempak, Kampung Paya Jaras Hilir, Kampung Paya Jaras Dalam, and the Selangor State Development Corporation (PKNS) Low-Cost Housing. Mohd Hafiz said following the incident, the main route connecting Kampung Kubu Gajah and Kampung Paya Jaras Hilir has been fully closed for safety reasons. He noted that the Petaling District Public Works Department (JKR) has provided alternative routes via Jalan Merbau Sempak from Federal Route 54 (FT54) to Kampung Kubu Gajah, as well as Jalan Paya Jaras Hilir from FT54 to Kampung Paya Jaras Hilir.

items.title: Google commits additional US$15b to Malaysia data centre expansion over two years, projects 37,000 jobs as Anwar hails investment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Google will invest an additional US$15 billion (RM61 billion) in Malaysia over the next two years to expand its data centre infrastructure, which is expected to contribute an annual average of US$1.1 billion to the country’s gross domestic product (GDP). Alphabet and Google president and chief investment officer Ruth Porat said the investment would cover the expansion of Google’s existing data centre campus at Elmina Business Park in Selangor, as well as new planned campuses in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan. Porat said the investment reflected Google’s confidence in Malaysia’s leadership, skilled workforce and commitment to digital transformation, while strengthening the company’s presence in the country and Southeast Asia.

items.title: Ramanan: Socso to pay RM174,000 in benefits to families of 28 Nepal-Tibet flood victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Twenty-eight out of the 54 victims of the flood tragedy in the Nepal-Tibet region on August 26 met the contribution eligibility requirements of Social Security Organisation (Socso), thereby entitling their next-of-kin to receive benefits. “Today, 16 families (out of the 28 eligible families) are present. Also present were Socso board chairman Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal and Socso group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr. Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed.

items.title: Tengku Zafrul says Malaysia’s RM431.1b approved investments reflect investor confidence as country courts new partnerships
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Malaysia highlighted opportunities for cooperation in the semiconductor, artificial intelligence (AI), digital infrastructure, clean energy and halal industries at the B57+ Business Leaders’ Summit 2026 in Istanbul, Türkiye. Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz said these sectors were among the potential areas for further exploration to strengthen economic cooperation between Malaysia and other countries. Tengku Zafrul also highlighted Malaysia’s investment performance, which recorded RM431.1 billion in approved investments in 2025 and RM218.5 billion in the first half of 2026.

items.title: Commuters, brace for a wet evening: MetMalaysia flags heavy storms nationwide until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a nationwide thunderstorm advisory for this evening, warning of torrential downpours, lightning, and gusty winds across Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah until 7.00pm today. The alert, released at 3.50pm, places the entirety of Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, and Perlis on high alert, alongside selected districts across several other states. The warning concurrently extends across Penang’s mainland districts of Seberang Perai Utara, Tengah, and Selatan, alongside nine Perak districts, including Kerian, Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Larut Matang, Selama, and Batang Padang.

items.title: Anwar says govt had previously rescued Utusan Malaysia publisher amid financial difficulties
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had previously stepped in to rescue the publisher of Utusan Malaysia and Kosmo! when the company faced operational difficulties. Anwar said this when asked whether the company’s rationalisation exercise was justified and whether the affected employees would receive compensation.

items.title: Kelantan eyes industrial hub, jobs and investment around ECRL station in Pasir Puteh
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 4 — The development of an East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) station in Cherang Tuli, Pasir Puteh, is expected to unlock greater economic opportunities through the influx of investments, job creation, business expansion, and increased income for local residents. Kelantan Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the state government will ensure that the area surrounding the ECRL corridor in Pasir Puteh is planned to accommodate industrial activities directly linked to the rail transport facility. He was responding to a question from Nor Asilah Mohamed Zin (PAS-Limbongan) regarding the state government’s plans to ensure that Pasir Puteh derives economic benefits from the ECRL development, during the Kelantan State Legislative Assembly sitting at the Kota Darulnaim Complex here today.

items.title: Kelantan records 2,135 Syariah arrests in three years, with khalwat cases topping list
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 4 — Kelantan recorded 2,135 arrests for offences under Islamic law between 2023 and 2025, with khalwat (close proximity) offences accounting for the highest number at 1,446 cases, the Kelantan State Legislative Assembly was told today. State Islamic Development, Dakwah, Information and Public Relations Committee chairman Mohd Asri Mat Daud said the statistics resulted from enforcement operations carried out by the Kelantan Islamic Religious Affairs Department (JAHEAIK) through its Syariah Law Enforcement Division. “Another 21 cases involved men impersonating women, three involved women impersonating men, three involved encouraging immoral activities, while 63 cases were related to other miscellaneous offences.

items.title: Fadhlina Sidek: Nearly 1,800 teachers denied permanent posts after failing key exam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4— A total of 1,799 education service officers (PPP) currently undergoing their probationary period have failed the prescribed examination for teachers, the Ministry of Education revealed in a written reply issued yesterday. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said failure in the comprehension assessment under the Mind Transformation Programme, known in Malay as Program Transformasi Minda (PTM) was the primary factor preventing these teachers from securing permanent service confirmation. Three officers had their probationary period extended with a penalty, 29 had their probationary period extended without penalty, and one officer had their probationary status frozen.

items.title: ‘No need to go to such extremes’: Azalina tells Hadi to drop ‘Dajjal’ label in CSA criticism
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang could have found better words than “Dajjal” to voice his opposition to the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) between Bersatu MPs and the government. The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said this when asked about Hadi’s statement yesterday, in which he likened the CSA to the Dajjal, The Star reported. Suhaimi is one of six Bersatu MPs who signed the CSA.

items.title: Hyrox Malaysia says ‘we got this wrong’, ends Carlsberg tie-up for KL race
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Hyrox Malaysia has apologised and said it will not extend its partnership with beer brand Carlsberg for its upcoming Hyrox Kuala Lumpur 2026 fitness race. The Youth and Sports Ministry had earlier today refused to approve the fitness event unless the organisers cut ties with the alcohol sponsor. In a statement posted on its Instagram account today, the organiser said the regional announcement naming Carlsberg as a partner had caused concern and offence.

items.title: ‘Do not abuse your popularity’: Judge delivers warning after preacher Da’i Syed beats rape charge in split decision
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 4 — A Court of Appeal judge has advised celebrity preacher Da’I Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, not to abuse his popularity or take advantage of vulnerable individuals. Syed Shah Iqmal, 31, who was standing in the dock, was seen nodding as he listened to the judge’s remarks. The panel made the decision after allowing Syed Shah Iqmal’s final appeal against his conviction and sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment and three strokes of the cane, imposed by the Shah Alam Sessions Court.

items.title: Putrajaya rejects foreign pressure to hike defence spending, maintains non-aligned stance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Malaysia is not obligated to heed the recommendation made by major powers to raise its defence spending to 5 per cent of Gross National Product (GNP), Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin told the Dewan Rakyat today. Khaled said Mindef will manage its defence budget based on its own national capabilities. Putrajaya allocates roughly 1.0 to 1.1 per cent of national output to defence spending annually, according to Malaysian Defence, an online defence magazine.

items.title: Former Sungai Ujong Undang and five others fail to halt contempt proceedings
items.summary: A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Amarjeet Singh unanimously dismissed the application and ordered the six appellants to pay RM60,000 in costs to the respondents, namely Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan (DKU) and its secretary, Raja Norazli Raja Nordin. The six applicants, comprising four Undangs and two chieftains, had appealed against the Seremban High Court’s decision granting the DKU and Raja Norazli leave to initiate committal proceedings against them for allegedly breaching an injunction order. The six appellants, besides Mubarak, are Undang Luak of Jelebu Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Undang Luak of Johol Datuk Muhammed Abdullah, Undang Luak of Rembau Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin, Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman Tunku Syed Idrus Al-Qadri, and Shahbandar of Sungai Ujong Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid.

items.title: Malaysia’s first female education D-G Asiah Abu Samah dies at 89
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Renowned education figure Tan Sri Dr Asiah Abu Samah died at a private hospital in the capital today. Asiah, the first woman to serve as Malaysia’s director-general of education, died at 5 am. Meanwhile, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek described Asiah’s passing as a major loss to the nation’s education sector, particularly given her contributions to the development of the national education system.

items.title: Penang Hospital to complete new blocks in 2027 and 2029 to tackle overcrowding
items.summary: He said the Health Ministry was also implementing measures under its patient flow management guidelines, including diverting non-emergency patients from the department through stronger primary healthcare services and better screening at entry points. Statistically, Gooi said the proportion of critical patients in the Red Zone rose to 7.14 per cent by July 2026, up from 6.79 per cent in 2025, while semi-critical Yellow Zone cases rose to 19.81 per cent from 18.92 per cent. Green Zone cases remained almost unchanged at 40.06 per cent, compared with 40.13 per cent in 2025, while non-emergency cases (LOCUM) declined to 32.99 per cent from 34.16 per cent, he added.
